deal.subIndustry: Independent community pharmacy with LTC/retirement home services (14 homes) and non-sterile compounding
deal.description: Independent specialty pharmacy in Ottawa, Ontario, founded in 2006 by owner-pharmacist Dr. Helen Park. Three service lines: community dispensing, contracted long-term care and retirement home services for 14 homes (1,046 beds, strip packaging, eMAR, 24/7 on-call) and NAPRA Level B non-sterile compounding including veterinary work. 23 staff. FY2024 revenue $9.12M, adjusted EBITDA $780K. Owner retiring; share sale, cash-free/debt-free.

overview.reason: Buyers need to understand reputation and patient trust in this relationship-driven business.

employees.reason: Pharmacist retention is critical; losing licensed staff post-close cripples operations immediately.

strengths.reason: Differentiators like compounding and LTC contracts directly impact competitive positioning and margins.

financials.reason: Buyers verify EBITDA adjustments and assess reimbursement pressure on margins.

operations.reason: Strip packaging systems and eMAR integration are expensive; buyers need operational continuity.

real_estate.reason: Lease terms and landlord consent are essential; relocation destroys patient base.

seasonality.reason: Prescription volume is relatively stable; minor flu-season variance doesn't affect valuation.

asking_price.reason: Valuation multiples and seller financing terms determine deal feasibility for pharmacist buyers.

buyer_profile.reason: Only licensed pharmacists can own in Ontario; narrows buyer pool significantly.

target_market.reason: Demographics and payer mix determine prescription volume stability and reimbursement risk.

reason_for_sale.reason: Buyers scrutinize whether retirement is real or masks LTC contract loss.

revenue_sources.reason: LTC contracts and compounding revenue concentration directly drive buyer risk assessment.

growth_potential.reason: Buyers assess whether LTC bed capacity and compounding volume can expand profitably.

permits_licenses.reason: Ontario pharmacy and compounding licenses must transfer; delays kill deals immediately.

training_support.reason: Owner's LTC relationships and compounding expertise require structured handover to preserve revenue.
